text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when calcium ions are actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, removing them from troponin and allowing tropomyosin to block myosin-binding sites on actin. This prevents cross-bridge formation, and the fibre returns to its resting length passively. The claim about a built-in safety mechanism that shuts down contraction when nerve signal intensity is too high is not accurate.
CONFIDENCE: 95
